text: Two rows with i & 1; one row when the order allows.

Rolling arrays (滚动数组): when row i of a DP only reads row i − 1, keep two rows and alternate with i & 1 (or i % 2). Memory drops from O(nm) to O(m). If row i reads only row i − 1 at positions ≤ j and the update order allows it, a single row is enough (0/1 knapsack loops j downward for exactly this reason, 进阶篇第13章).
What is lost: you can no longer reconstruct the choices from the table. Keep the full table (or store decisions separately) when the problem asks for the actual solution, not just its value.

f[cur][0] stays 0 for every row because column 0 is never written: no reset is needed. In general, reset the row you are about to overwrite if some entries are not assigned.
Digits 0/1/2; pow3 tables.

Base-3 state compression (三进制状压): when each item has three states (unused / used once / used twice, or empty / white / black), encode the state as a number in base 3: digit i is item i's state. There are 3ⁿ states; precompute pow3[i] and, if needed, the digit table digit[s][i] for every state.
Bits do not work here because a digit needs values 0, 1, 2. Reading digit i: s / pow3[i] % 3; changing it from d to d + 1: s + pow3[i]. With n = 10 there are 59 049 states, fine for O(3ⁿ · n²).

Visit every city at least once and at most twice, starting anywhere, with the smallest total cost. Adding pw[j] always makes a larger number, so increasing s is a valid order. Checked against a Python Dijkstra over (city, visit counts).
Count-based states are another way to avoid big masks: 中国象棋(P2051) only needs how many columns hold 0, 1 or 2 pieces, not which ones.
Rectangles as states; board splitting.

Two-dimensional interval DP (二维区间 DP): the state is a rectangle f[k][x1][y1][x2][y2], built from smaller rectangles. Board splitting (棋盘分割 P5752): cut the board straight across, keep one side, and continue cutting the other; after n − 1 cuts minimise the variance of the n pieces' sums.

Variance = (Σ (sᵢ − avg)²) / n with avg fixed (total / n), so minimising Σ (sᵢ − avg)² is enough. Each cut is horizontal or vertical, and either side may be the one cut further: 4 choices per cut position. Rectangle sums come from 2D prefix sums.

Key points to memorise
1. Row i reads only row i − 1 ⇒ two rows with i & 1 (or one row with the right order).
2. Rolling arrays lose the path: keep decisions if you must print it.
3. Base 3: digit = s / 3^i % 3; increment = s + 3^i; 3^10 ≈ 6·10⁴.
4. 2D interval DP: f[k][x1][y1][x2][y2]; cut across, 4 choices per cut position.
5. Variance with fixed mean: minimise Σ (s − avg)².
